data.name: eIF4A

identifiers_status.reason: This record names a complex, a protein family or a pair of proteins, so one gene identifier would claim more than the Atlas knows.

data.description: ATP-dependent RNA helicase that unwinds 5' mRNA secondary structures; activated downstream of mTORC1 to promote selective cap-dependent translation initiation.

page_status.reason: By design: fewer than three linked studies and not a node on the pathway map, so no page is generated. The record is still served here and in the bulk exports.

data.description_beginner: A protein 'motor' that unwinds tangled sections of mRNA so the cell's protein-building machinery can read through them. mTORC1 activity switches this motor on to help build proteins faster.

studies.title: Redox-sensitive mTOR-eIF4A signaling promotes selective P-glycoprotein translation.
studies.authors: Jin P; Jin M; Feng L; He J; Yin Y; Bai R; Feng T; Zhang T; Luo H; Ma X; Chen J; Hussain S; Wan S; Fang Z; Wu Y; Luo L

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Oxidative stress activates a redox-sensitive PI3K-AKT-mTORC1-eIF4A cascade that selectively promotes P-glycoprotein translation via cap-dependent mRNA engagement, revealing a transcription-independent mechanism of rapid multidrug resistance induction.
